why: Names the Seven Speakers who won the Faithful for Jaehaerys and Alysanne.
Describes the Butcher's Ball fight on a ridge but never names Crossed Elms.
States Vermithor bent his neck to blacksmith's bastard Hugh the Hammer, or Hard Hugh.
Names the three council lords who died, but not the replacements (Rodrik Arryn, Martyn Tyrell).
Covers Rhaenyra's grief after Lucerys, but not her hardened heart or resolve for fire and blood.
States Addam came to prove his loyalty by destroying the Two Betrayers and their dragons, riding Seasmoke.
States the Widow's Law reaffirmed inheritance and required heirs to maintain widows; rank 2 ties it to the women's courts.
States the firstborn daughter would be fostered at Winterfell to marry Cregan's heir; rank 1 names the pact.
Covers the false murder rumor, but not the riot or the Storming of the Dragonpit.
Describes her cooking from within, but neither the worms nor Barth's Valyria theory.
Says Vhagar was the last of Aegon's three dragons, but no passage covers the battle or her death.
Says Larys ordered Aegon II's death and Aegon the Younger arrived, but not the betrayal of the greens.

Mystery of the social order, and equality with Heaven prevents the rich being massacred; rank 4 has the vaccine.
Rule by civil qualities and a nation united by property outweighs soldiers; rank 3 says the civilian sees the common good.
No social revolution without terror; terror is an inevitable phase (volcano image absent).
Dreamers seeking a general constitutional pattern who ignore human character; power rests on material strength.
Loves power as a musician loves his violin, for sounds, chords and harmonies.
None covers his intentions being cleared by the necessity of dictatorship against anarchy.
Says men are moved by two levers only: fear and self-interest.
Political testament passages are about other things; equality and love of distinctions never appear.

Shows he read 'your grandfather's book' cover to cover (rank 4 names Necker), but not the title.

Larrey, his surgeon general, 'the most virtuous man I have ever known'.
Says he made the Moniteur the soul and chief strength of his government.
States the sum of six thousand francs for electricity and galvanism.
'An agreed-upon fiction', with material fact and moral intent.
'I come from Nantes in Brittany.'

This sacred squadron, commanded by General Grouchy.
Supports the second party because the rich owners and priests can win over the masses.
Duroc, the man he loved most, and how quickly he moved on; rank 2 has the bulletin and 'another life'.
Calculating all possibilities, then an almost exact allowance for accident; a decimal may alter everything.

Believers not reasoners; weakness of brains and mobility of ideas need resignation through a charitable religion.
